title: deploy-misconfig flags env-backed defaults, parse bases and docs strings as hard-coded URLs
symptom: deploy-misconfig flags several non-defect URL literals as hard-coded local URLs: (1) env-backed defaults like process.env.X ?? "http://localhost:8000" — the exact remediation the rule suggests; (2) test-tooling files (playwright.config.ts, e2e/*) where a localhost target is the point; (3) docs/snippet strings (a <pre> install block, an env-file example rendered in the UI); (4) `new URL(path, "http://x")` parse bases; (5) `http://${var}` template builders.
expected: URL literals behind process.env/environment/.default(), inside new URL() bases, http://${} builders, docs strings and test-tooling files are not flagged.
regression_test: vitest: scanner/src/rules.test.ts (clean-app zero-findings gate + FP-class coverage checks)
root_cause: The rule flagged every localhost/http URL literal without checking whether it was already env-backed, a parse base, a template builder, docs text, or in test tooling.
bench_note: Multiple literal-shape escapes on one rule; regression is the clean-app FP-coverage files plus zero-findings gate.
notes: Found while scanning real repos for the case-study hunt — the scanner's own false positives are registered before fixing, per the issue-register rule.
